answer_1.quote: Our goal is to generate a natural language summary which articulates S_e, the set of selected opinions...We describe our framework...and present two types of experiments...a quantitative comparison...and two user studies, validating the automatic results and our method's ability for controllable summarization.

answer_2.quote: We performed automatic evaluation on the YELP dataset with ROUGE-1 (R1), ROUGE-2 (R2), and ROUGE-L (RL) scores based on the 200 reference summaries.

answer_4.quote: We conducted three user studies to evaluate the quality of the generated summaries... Best-Worst Scaling Task... we asked the annotators to select the best and worst summaries w.r.t. the following criteria: Informativeness, Coherence, Non-redundancy... Content Support Task... judges evaluated whether each summary sentence was fully, partially, or not supported... Aspect-Specific Summary Task... judges judged whether the summaries discussed the specified aspect exclusively, partially, or not at all. We used crowdsourcing via the FigureEight platform.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to judge summaries based on informativeness, coherence, non-redundancy (best-worst), content support level (full/partial/none), and aspect coverage (exclusive/partial/none).
